data.narrative:
Quobly is a seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Maud Vinet, Tristan Meunier, and François Perruchot. The quantum computing sector includes 11 identifiable peers: 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms, with notable private players including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The quantum computing peer set, while containing 6 same-sector companies, yields zero matches when filtered to same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier cohorts—falling short of the minimum three datapoints required for reliable triangulation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial distortion given the wide dispersion in maturity and capital intensity across the peer universe.

Without sufficient narrow-stage comparables, traditional multiples-based approaches cannot be reliably deployed. A defensible valuation would require alternative methods such as venture-backed cost-of-capital approaches, venture capital method back-solving from hypothetical exit scenarios, or deep-dive operational and technology benchmarking against the broader peer set. The seed stage and nascent nature of the quantum hardware and software market present meaningful uncertainty in scaling assumptions and competitive positioning. Any valuation estimate at this stage should be framed as indicative pending either (i) accumulation of operational milestones that enable comparability to more mature-stage peers, or (ii) explicit first-principles analysis of development pathway and capital requirements.
